34825-she-buildeth-her-house.title: She Buildeth Her House
34825-she-buildeth-her-house.creator: Unknown
34825-she-buildeth-her-house.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Reifferscheid, though not one of the giants, found Paula a distraction in brown, when she entered his office before nine in the morning, during the fall of 1901. He edited the rather distinguished weekly book-page of _The States_, and had come to rely upon her for a paper or two in each issue. There had been rain in the night. The mellow October sunlight was strange with that same charm of maturity which adds a glow of attraction to motherhood.

arxiv-2107-08965.title: Maximizing Nash Social Welfare in 2-Value Instances
arxiv-2107-08965.creator: Hannaneh Akrami, Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Martin Hoefer, Kurt Mehlhorn, Marco Schmalhofer, Golnoosh Shahkarami, Giovanna Varricchio, Quentin Vermande, Ernest van Wijland
arxiv-2107-08965.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hannaneh Akrami, Bhaskar Ray Chaudhury, Martin Hoefer, Kurt Mehlhorn, Marco Schmalhofer, Golnoosh Shahkarami, Giovanna Varricchio, Quentin Vermande, Ernest van Wijland. We consider the problem of maximizing the Nash social welfare when allocating a set 𝒢 {\cal G} of indivisible goods to a set 𝒩 {\cal N} of agents.

arxiv-2111-04050.title: Entropy production and correlation spreading in the interaction between particle detector and thermal baths
arxiv-2111-04050.creator: Hao Xu, Si Yu Chen
arxiv-2111-04050.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Hao Xu, Si Yu Chen. Entropy production is the key to the second law of thermodynamics, and it is well defined by considering a joint unitary evolution of a system S S and a thermal environment E E . However, due to the diversity of the initial state and Hamiltonian of the system and environment, it is hard to evaluate the characterisation of entropy production.

arxiv-2206-15437.title: Understanding Instance-Level Impact of Fairness Constraints
arxiv-2206-15437.creator: Jialu Wang, Xin Eric Wang, Yang Liu
arxiv-2206-15437.description: Abstract A variety of fairness constraints have been proposed in the literature to mitigate group-level statistical bias. Their impacts have been largely evaluated for different groups of populations corresponding to a set of sensitive attributes, such as race or gender. Nonetheless, the community has not observed sufficient explorations for how imposing fairness constraints fare at an instance level.

arxiv-2302-13966.title: Hydrodynamic instabilities in a 2-D sheet of microswimmers embedded in a 3-D fluid
arxiv-2302-13966.creator: Viktor Škultéty 1, Dóra Bárdfalvy 2, Joakim Stenhammar 2, Cesare Nardini 3, Alexander Morozov 1
arxiv-2302-13966.description: Abstract A collection of microswimmers immersed in an incompressible fluid is characterised by strong interactions due to the long-range nature of the hydrodynamic fields generated by individual organisms. As a result, suspensions of rear-actuated ‘pusher’ swimmers such as bacteria exhibit a collective motion state often referred to as ‘bacterial turbulence’, characterised by large-scale chaotic flows.

arxiv-2304-13775.title: Advancing Ischemic Stroke Diagnosis: A Novel Two-Stage Approach for Blood Clot Origin Identification
arxiv-2304-13775.creator: Koushik Sivarama Krishnan 1 , Joe Nikesh Puthota John 2 , Swathi Gnanasekar 3 , Karthik Sivarama Krishnan 4
arxiv-2304-13775.description: Abstract An innovative two-stage methodology for categorizing blood clot origins is presented in this paper, which is important for the diagnosis and treatment of ischemic stroke. First, a background classifier based on MobileNetV3 segments big whole-slide digital pathology images into numerous tiles to detect the presence of cellular material.

arxiv-2307-09494.title: Explanation-Guided Fair Federated Learning for Transparent 6G RAN Slicing Thanks: S. Roy is with Iquadrat Informatica S.L. and Technical University of Catalonia (UPC), Barcelona, Spain, H. Chergui is with i2CAT Foundation, Barcelona, Spain and C. Verikoukis is with ATHENA/ISI and University of Patra
arxiv-2307-09494.creator: Swastika Roy, Hatim Chergui
arxiv-2307-09494.description: Abstract Future zero-touch artificial intelligence (AI)-driven 6G network automation requires building trust in the AI black boxes via explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), where it is expected that AI faithfulness would be a quantifiable service-level agreement (SLA) metric along with telecommunications key performance indicators (KPIs). This entails exploiting the XAI outputs to generate transparent and unbiased deep neural networks (DNNs).

arxiv-2311-14000.title: Challenges and limitations of future exoplanet space imagers
arxiv-2311-14000.creator: L. Leboulleux
arxiv-2311-14000.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by L. Leboulleux. The James Webb Space Telescope was not even launched yet when the Astro2020 Decadal Survey American report recommended the development of what is now called the Habitable World Observatory, also mentioned by the Voyage 2050 European report.

arxiv-2401-00517.title: Detecting Imprinting and Maternal Effects Using Monte Carlo Expectation Maximization Algorithm
arxiv-2401-00517.creator: Pooya Aavani, Alexandre Trindade, Fangyuan Zhang
arxiv-2401-00517.description: Abstract Numerous statistical methods have been developed to explore genomic imprinting and maternal effects, which are causes of parent-of-origin patterns in complex human diseases. However, most of them either only model one of these two confounded epigenetic effects, or make strong yet unrealistic assumptions about the population to avoid over- parameterization.

arxiv-2401-07383.title: Recent mathematical advances in coupled cluster theory
arxiv-2401-07383.creator: Fabian M. Faulstich
arxiv-2401-07383.description: Abstract This article presents an in-depth educational overview of the latest mathematical developments in coupled cluster (CC) theory, beginning with Schneider’s seminal work from 2009 that introduced the first local analysis of CC theory. We offer a tutorial review of second quantization and the CC ansatz, laying the groundwork for understanding the mathematical basis of the theory.

arxiv-2408-14481.title: Formalization of Operational Domain and Operational Design Domain for Automated Vehicles
arxiv-2408-14481.creator: Ali Shakeri
arxiv-2408-14481.description: Abstract Specifying an Operational Design Domain (ODD) is crucial for safeguarding automated vehicle systems against conditions that exceed their capabilities. Yet, prior definitions of ODD have relied on ambiguous and unclear terms, resulting in numerous misunderstandings and misconceptions. This paper introduces a formal approach to clearly define the Operational Domain (OD) and ODD for automated vehicles.

arxiv-2410-04740.title: Evaluating the Generalization Ability of Spatiotemporal Model in Urban Scenario Thanks: Hongjun Wang, Jiyuan Chen, Tong Pan, Zheng Dong and Lingyu Zhang are with (1) SUSTech-UTokyo Joint Research Center on Super Smart City, Department of Computer Science and Engineering (2) Research Institute of Tru
arxiv-2410-04740.creator: Hongjun Wang, Jiyuan Chen, Tong Pan, Zheng Dong
arxiv-2410-04740.description: Abstract Spatiotemporal neural networks have shown great promise in urban scenarios by effectively capturing temporal and spatial correlations. However, urban environments are constantly evolving, and current model evaluations are often limited to traffic scenarios and use data mainly collected only a few weeks after training period to evaluate model performance. The generalization ability of these models remains largely unexplored.

arxiv-2410-09534.title: SUS-Lib: An automated tool for usability evaluation based on the Software Usability Scale from user feedback
arxiv-2410-09534.creator: Paweł Weichbroth, Małgorzata Giedrowicz
arxiv-2410-09534.description: Abstract Usability evaluation has received considerable attention from both the research and practice communities. While there are many evaluation tools available, the Software Usability Scale (SUS) is the most widely used. In this paper, we introduce and describe the SUS-Lib software package, which aims to compute SUS scores and generate graphical figures based on user input.

arxiv-2411-09715.title: Two Colored Diagrams for Central Configurations of the Planar Five-vortex Problem
arxiv-2411-09715.creator: Xiang Yu, Shuqiang Zhu
arxiv-2411-09715.description: Abstract We apply the singular sequence method to investigate the finiteness problem for stationary configurations of the planar five-vortex problem. The initial step of the singular sequence method involves identifying all two-colored diagrams. These diagrams represent potential scenarios where finiteness may fail. We determined all such diagrams for the planar five-vortex problem.

arxiv-2501-19266.title: Jackpot! Alignment as a Maximal Lottery
arxiv-2501-19266.creator: Roberto-Rafael Maura-Rivero, Marc Lanctot, Francesco Visin, Kate Larson
arxiv-2501-19266.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), the standard for aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human values, is known to fail to satisfy properties that are intuitively desirable, such as respecting the preferences of the majority ( Ge et al., 2024 ) .

pmc-10573162.title: Enhancing Lower Extremity Defect Coverage: High Viability Ultra-Thin Split-Thickness Skin Grafts Obtained from the Scalp
pmc-10573162.creator: Alejandra Tomás-Velázquez, Javier Antoñanzas, Rafael Salido-Vallejo, Pedro Redondo
pmc-10573162.description: Background: Repairing lower extremity defects presents challenges due to the scarcity of available local tissue. Skin grafting is a widely employed technique for addressing non-healing ulcers, improving the quality of life of patients and minimizing discomfort. However, using traditional donor sites, such as the thigh, can hinder mobility and result in noticeable scarring and pigmentation changes.

pmc-10612089.title: Epidemiology Update of Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) in Uruguay: Subtyping, Environmental Surveillance and Zoonotic Transmission
pmc-10612089.creator: Florencia Cancela, Romina Icasuriaga, Santiago Cuevas, Valentina Hergatacorzian, Mauricio Olivera, Yanina Panzera, Ruben Pérez, Julieta López, Liliana Borzacconi, Elizabeth González, Natalia Montaldo, Melissa Gaitán, Sandra López-Verges, Viviana Bortagaray, Matías Victoria, Rodney Colina, Juan Arbiz
pmc-10612089.description: Hepatitis E Virus (HEV) infection is an emergent zoonotic disease of increasing concern in developed regions. HEV genotype 3 (HEV-3) is mainly transmitted through consumption of contaminated food in high-income countries and is classified into at least 13 subtypes (3a–3n), based on p-distance values from complete genomes. In Latin America, HEV epidemiology studies are very scant.

pmc-12442325.title: Supporting linkage facilitators working with persons with opioid use disorder: challenges, advances, and future directions
pmc-12442325.creator: Tess K. Drazdowski, Anthony P. Coetzer-Liversage, L. A. R. Stein, Martha Tilson, Dennis P. Watson, Lauren A. Hoffman, Aaron Hogue, Sierra Castedo de Martell, Angela Marie Hagaman, R. Neil Greene, Milan F. Satcher, Patrick F. Hibbard, Jodie M. Dewey, Ashli J. Sheidow, Noel Vest
pmc-12442325.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This narrative review explores the evolving role of linkage facilitation (LF) in supporting persons with opioid use disorder (OUD) including both the organizational strategies to initiate and sustain LF services and strategies to support the LF workforce. Drawing on expert consensus and iterative review by an interdisciplinary author team, we synthesized relevant literature from diverse fields using a narrative review approach.

pmc-12525475.title: Identification of Proteins and MicroRNAs with Prognostic Value for Assisted Reproduction Technology Outcomes in Follicular Fluid of Women with Endometriosis: A Pilot Study
pmc-12525475.creator: Ana Catarina Neto, Cláudia Freitas, Ângela Ribeiro, Adriana R Rodrigues, João L Silva-Carvalho, Henrique Almeida, Delminda Neves, Daniel Vaiman
pmc-12525475.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This study aims to identify molecular markers with prognostic value for biochemical pregnancy in follicular fluid (FF) samples from women with endometriosis after assisted reproductive technology (ART) intervention. Levels of growth differentiation factor-9 (GDF-9), bone morphogenetic protein-15 (BMP-15), and anti-Mullerian hormone (AMH) proteins were semi-quantified by Western blotting and microRNAs 20a_1, 145_1, 320a_1, 125-b-5p, 212-3p, and 199_a by qPCR in FF samples from women submitted to ART with a previous diagnosis of endometriosis (n = 20) or male factor infertility (controls) (n

pmc-12578635.title: A host-directed adjuvant sensitizes intracellular bacterial persisters to antibiotics
pmc-12578635.creator: Kuan-Yi Lu, Xiangbo Yang, Matthew J G Eldridge, Rongfeng Sun, Rachel T Giorgio, Benjamin I Morris, Nikki J Wagner, Brian Hardy, Matthew Axtman, Sarah E Rowe, Xiaodong Wang, Vance G Fowler, Qingyun Liu, Sophie Helaine, Kenneth H Pearce, Brian P Conlon
pmc-12578635.description: Intracellular bacterial reservoirs contribute to antibiotic treatment failure by fostering metabolically dormant persister cells that are highly tolerant to killing. However, strategies to effectively target intracellular persister cells remain limited. Here we developed a high-throughput screen to identify compounds that modulate the metabolic activity of intracellular Staphylococcus aureus.

pmc-12592781.title: Assessing a Stimulator Modification for Simultaneous Noninvasive Auricular Vagus Nerve Stimulation and MRI
pmc-12592781.creator: Vanessa Teckentrup, Mareike Ludwig, Janis Seibt, Renée Hartig, Hubert Preissl, Mark Schuppert, Nikolai I Avdievich, Klaus Scheffler, Nikos Priovoulos, Maik Ehses, Benedikt A Poser, Christopher J Wiggins, Peter Trautner, Walter Honerbach, Heidi I L Jacobs, Oliver Speck, Dorothea Hämmerer, Nils B Kroe
pmc-12592781.description: Background and PurposeThe vagus nerve can be stimulated noninvasively at the ear using transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS). Concurrent functional MRI (fMRI) permits study of taVNS‐induced changes in brain dynamics, a key requisite for precision neurostimulation. However, there is no standardized protocol for how to safely apply taVNS during MRI.

pmc-12913795.title: Hair hormone profiling as a non-invasive diagnostic approach for assessing long-term endocrine status and productivity in Hereford bulls
pmc-12913795.creator: Alexey Frolov, Oleg Zavyalov, Zulfiya Galieva
pmc-12913795.description: Background and Aim:Accurate evaluation of hormonal status is critical for optimizing growth performance and meat quality in beef cattle. Conventional matrices such as blood, saliva, and urine reflect only short-term fluctuations and are influenced by collection stress. Hair, as a retrospective biosubstrate, can integrate hormone secretion over time and serve as a non-invasive indicator of chronic endocrine activity.

pmc-13247105.title: Acute brain dysfunction clusters in COVID-19: a pilot machine learning-based analysis of the COVID-D cohort
pmc-13247105.creator: Nekane Romero-García, Víctor Montosa-i-Micó, David Fernández-Narro, Juan M. García-Gómez, Luis Hurtado, Eduardo Passariello, Fabio Silvio Taccone, Chiara Robba, Rameela Raman, Onur M. Orun, Pratik Pandharipande, Brenda T. Pun, E. Wesley Ely, Rafael Badenes, Carlos Sáez
pmc-13247105.description: PurposeWhile acute brain dysfunction (ABD, i.e., delirium and coma) is associated with significantly increased morbidity in critically ill patients, it presents with great heterogeneity that poses a challenge for management and prognostication. While machine learning may be promising for subgroup identification, this approach has not yet been applied to COVID-19 patients with ABD.
